description:
Add F# as a first-class supported language in Catseye.

Approach
- Ship a small .NET console app `fsharp-extractor` (mirroring the Crystal/Elixir extractor pattern) that uses `FSharp.Compiler.Service` (FCS) to parse `.fs`, `.fsx`, `.fsi` files and emit a stable XML representation of the AST + key typed symbols.
- Add a Catseye plugin (`catseye_ast/fsharp_plugin.ml` + `fsharp_mapper.ml`) that consumes that wire format and produces `CatseyeAST.t`, so the rest of the pipeline (IL, CFG, taint, code smells) needs no F#-specific changes.
- Update `flake.nix` to add `dotnet-sdk` to the dev shell and wire the extractor build.

Why FCS (not tree-sitter-fsharp)
- FCS gives a *typed* AST (resolves names, types, symbols). tree-sitter-fsharp gives only an untyped CST.
- We already have the "external extractor" pattern for Crystal and Elixir; F# fits it cleanly.

First-slice scope (taint)
- Sources: `Console.ReadLine`, `Console.In.ReadLine`, `System.Environment.GetCommandLineArgs`, `System.Console.ReadKey`.
- Sinks: `System.Console.Write/WriteLine`, `printf/eprintf/fprintf`, `System.IO.File.WriteAllText/AppendAllLines/WriteAllLines`, `System.Diagnostics.Process.Start`, `System.Net.Http.HttpClient.PostAsync/SendAsync/GetStringAsync`, `System.Net.WebClient.DownloadString`.
- Skip: `ignore`, `id`, `failwith`, `invalidArg`.
- Manifest files: `*.fsproj`, `paket.dependencies`.
- This is intentionally a small first slice — easy to grow.

Out of scope (non-goals)
- F# scripting REPL analysis (`.fsx` is parsed, not executed).
- Full F# type-checker integration (we use the AST + symbols, not full type-checked IL).
- Building a separate `fsharp-crowsnest` or `fsharp-rules` package — F# goes through the existing pipeline.
- .NET dependency in production builds of the OCaml binary (extractor is a sidecar).
title: Add F# analysis using F# Compiler Service
